text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Life insurer Generali and building materials firm Brentjens complain to EU about Dutch law obliging companies to take part in sector pension funds. (p1)
- Liberal Party (VVD) leader says shareholders should have greater influence in running companies. (p1)
- Semiconductor firm ASMI to float on Amsterdam bourse on December 12. (p1)
- Social affairs and finance ministers differ on budget deficit. (p1)
- Car dealer AIR issues preference shares as protection against hostile takeover. (p3)
- Service union gives temp agency Randstad one week in which to change to paying net wages rather than gross. (p3)
- Engineering consultant to sell bulk of its environmental division to ENSR of the U.S. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Government blocked competition on Dutch telecoms market for years, says researcher. (p1)
- Coffee roaster Drie Mollen rounds off takeover of three European rivals. (p2)
- State printer SDU takes over legal publisher Koninklijke Vermande of Lelystad. (p2)
- Unilever only gets 80.6 pct of Irish tea producer Lyons Irish. (p19)
DE TELEGRAAF
- French police arrest notorious Dutch drugs baron. (p1)
- Dispensing chemists' organisation KNMP and health insurer Zilveren Kruis agree new contracts for pharmaceutical help. (p7)
- Dutch office building market emerging from slump. (p27)
- Utility company Nuon's Telekabel unit buys cable network in Zoetermeer. (p29)
TROUW
- Beter Bed shares jump to 30.6 guilders after launch. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Fokker Services will not pay to repair electronics fault in its F-70 and F-100 aircraft. (p11)
- Retailer Macintosh expects full year profit to drop dramatically. (p11)
